speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the onset and progression of your symptoms: when did the double vision, stair-climbing difficulty, and upper limb weakness first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with eye movement issues, strongly suggests a neuromuscular disorder. REQUEST TEST: AChR antibodies and MuSK antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation. Do these symptoms affect your ability to hold a cup or brush your teeth?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ocular symptoms (diplopia worsening with gaze), ptosis (implied by difficulty looking up/down), proximal muscle weakness, fatigability that improves with rest, and positive AChR antibodies with decreased response on repetitive nerve stimulation is diagnostic. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT scan to evaluate for thymoma.
